HYPOTHESIS (natural-language, data-grounded):

During the Younger Bronze Age, the first principal component of the twelve forms of capital is markedly higher at the opening horizon of 1100 BCE than at any subsequent horizon: PC1(1100 BCE) = +2.36 score units, versus a mean of +0.75 (range +0.41 to +1.14) for the six horizons from 1000 to 500 BCE — a difference of +1.61 PC1 units (+1.22 vs 1000 BCE, the nearest later horizon, widening to +1.95 vs 500 BCE). With a later-six standard deviation of only 0.30, 1100 BCE is an outlier (≈ +5.3 z-units), not a point on the continuum: after 1100 the scores form a smooth, monotonic decline from +1.14 (1000) through +0.86/+1.01 (900/800) to +0.41–0.43 (600/500). We therefore hypothesize that the beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) represents a distinct, elevated "capital peak" — driven above all by a surge in metal deposition/hoarding (ZHort = +3.38, the single strongest genuinely new signal at 1100, up from −0.33 at 1200) and, importantly, by the carry-over of late Old Bronze Age (OBA) peak values into the 1100 slice — after which all forms of capital settle into a lower, gradually declining regime through 500 BCE.

CAVEAT carried into the hypothesis (per instruction C): part of the 1100-vs-later contrast is a legacy of sparse-observation carry-over rather than an independent YBA signal. Seven of the twelve variables at 1100 BCE repeat the 1200 BCE value exactly (ZCU_AU = 2.85, Zhausgr = 1.65, ZMonument = 1.352, Zamber = −0.58, ZBeil = −1.05, ZKeform = −1.13, Zkeverz = 0.97), because one observation spans the 1200→1100 block. Of the gross positive contributions to the contrast, roughly three-quarters come from such carried-over variables — ZCU_AU (share ≈ 36% of gross positive contributions, the largest single driver), Zhausgr (≈ 14%), ZMonument (≈ 12%) — whereas the strongest genuinely new YBA observation is ZHort (≈ 24%, the hoard/depot surge at 1100 that persists at 3.38 into 1000 BCE). So the correct reading is: 1100 BCE is elevated relative to 1000–500 both because YBA-open values inherited a late-OBA metal/monument/house-size peak and because of a real new rise in hoarding; from 1000 BCE onward the capital system relaxes to a lower, slowly declining level.

KEY NUMBERS:
- Primary PCA (full 39-slice fit, 12 standardized Z-variables, numpy correlation-matrix eigendecomposition): PC1 explains 30.3% of variance (PC2 19.5%).
- Sign convention (stated): loadings flipped so that their sum is positive (flip WAS applied); higher PC1 = higher overall capital intensity weighted by these loadings. PC1 is bimodal in structure: positive on ZCU_AU (+0.41, social), Zkeverz (+0.38, cultural), ZHort (+0.34, economic), ZAxtSchwert (+0.30, symbolic), ZDolch (+0.27, symbolic), ZMW (+0.24, economic), Zhausgr (+0.23, symbolic), ZMonument (+0.20, social); negative on ZKeform (−0.35, cultural), ZBeil (−0.24, economic), Zamber (−0.24, social), ZSichel (−0.15, economic).
- PC1 by YBA horizon (score units): 1100: +2.362; 1000: +1.141; 900: +0.864; 800: +1.006; 700: +0.651; 600: +0.425; 500: +0.413.
- Differences 1100 vs each later horizon: +1.221 (1000), +1.498 (900), +1.356 (800), +1.711 (700), +1.937 (600), +1.948 (500); vs later-six mean: +1.612.
- Per-variable contributions (loading × value difference, unnormalized, later-mean baseline): ZCU_AU +1.17, ZHort +0.79, Zhausgr +0.46, ZDolch +0.42, ZMonument +0.38, Zkeverz −0.21 (the only material negative: pottery decoration is actually HIGHER in 1000–500 than at 1100, slightly offsetting the contrast); all others ≈ 0.
- Sensitivity (YBA-only PCA, constant ZKeform and ZSichel dropped, 10 vars, PC1 = 62.5% of variance): 1100 = +2.31 vs later mean −0.39 (diff +2.70); corr(PC1_full, PC1_ybaonly) = 0.992 over the 7 slices — the contrast is robust to the choice of reference covariance.
- Descriptive only (n = 7), no significance testing, as agreed.

WORKFLOW: (1) loaded capital.csv (decimal commas), 39 rows × 12 Z-columns, complete; (2) verified equivalence with time_series_data.csv at all 84 YBA horizon cells (max |diff| = 0.0), confirming slices = horizon values; (3) standardized all 12 Z-columns over the full 39-slice series; (4) PCA via eigendecomposition of the correlation matrix (numpy-only; sklearn unavailable in this runtime — mathematically identical to sklearn PCA on standardized data); (5) sign-fixed loadings (sum positive), extracted standardized PC1 scores at the 7 YBA horizons; (6) computed the 1100-vs-each-later and 1100-vs-mean contrasts, per-variable contributions, later-six spread, and a YBA-only sensitivity PCA dropping zero-variance columns; (7) exported scores and loadings as CSV artifacts.

payload.hypothesis: PC1 of the twelve forms of capital is an extreme outlier at the opening YBA horizon of 1100 BCE (+2.36 score units) relative to the 1000-500 BCE horizons (mean +0.75, range +0.41 to +1.14; contrast +1.61 units, ~+5.3 z-units vs the later-six spread); the later horizons form a monotonic declining continuum. The 1100 peak reflects both a genuine surge in metal hoarding (ZHort -0.33 -> +3.38, the strongest new YBA signal) and inherited late-OBA block values (ZCU_AU, Zhausgr, ZMonument carry over from 1200 BCE and account for roughly three-quarters of the gross positive contributions), after which the capital system relaxes and slowly declines through 500 BCE.
payload.workflow: capital.csv (39 hundred-year slices, 12 complete Z-columns) standardized; PCA on the full series via numpy eigendecomposition of the correlation matrix (sklearn unavailable); PC1 sign fixed by positive loadings sum; PC1 scores extracted for the 7 YBA horizons (1100-500 BCE); contrasts vs each later horizon and vs the later-six mean computed; per-variable contributions mapped to symbolic/social/cultural/economic forms; sensitivity PCA on YBA-only rows (constant ZKeform, ZSichel dropped) confirming the contrast (corr 0.992). Carry-over from 1200 BCE flagged: 7 of 12 variables repeat OBA block values at 1100; only ZHort is an independent new observation driving the peak. Descriptive contrast only (n=7).
